newsitem.title: CANADA: RTRS-Molson shares slump as Coors deal falls flat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Molson shares slump as Coors deal falls flat.

text.p: Molson Cos Ltd shares sank on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday after the Canadian brewing and sports firm lost an arbitration ruling over its licensing deal with U.S. beermaker Adolph Coors Co.
Molson class A stock fell 1.05 to 19.85 on 159,000 shares. The company's class B shares dropped 1.10 to 20.

A Canadian arbitration panel ruled over the weekend that Molson Breweries relinquished all rights to brew and distribute Coors products in 1993 when Miller Brewing Co, a unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc, bought an ownership interest in the Canadian brewer.
Molson Breweries, Canada's biggest brewer, is owned 40-percent each by Molson Cos Ltd and Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd and 20-percent by Miller Brewing.
The three-member panel found that Molson breached its licensing agreement with Coors by allowing Miller to acquire a 20 percent equity interest in Molson without Coors' consent.
In addition, the panel ordered Molson Breweries to repay to Coors the profits from the sale of Coors brands in Canada since April 2, 1993.
Molson said a specific amount has not been determined yet, but the impact on its earnings will be material.
Molson said it is prepared to work with Coors to address the U.S. brewer's concerns. Both companies have agreed to discuss the possibility of a new arrangement, he said.

"The negative impact on Molson Breweries' level of profit will not be known until these discussions are concluded, but it will be material," John Barnett, Molson Breweries' president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

In the interim, both parties have agreed that Molson will continue to produce and sell Coors brands in Canada. Coors brands account for about eight percent of Molson Breweries' total annual sales volume of 20 million hectoliters.
Molson Breweries' net income slipped to C$59.4 million in the first quarter ended July 1 from C$60.4 million in the same period a year earlier.
First quarter revenue was relatively flat at C$589.6 million, compared to C$590.1 million in the first quarter of last year.
